target: Exact German 1888 Naumann item witness for Der Fall Wagner

mdz_immediate_pdf.page_mapping: PDF page 1 is an MDZ-generated bibliographic cover; PDF pages 2-75 map one-to-one and in order to IIIF canvases 1-74.

observations: Canvas 1 is the red Bamberg holding binding and canvas 2 carries call number 30.1972.
Canvas 5 is the historical title page: Der Fall Wagner, Ein Musikanten-Problem, Friedrich Nietzsche, Leipzig, Verlag von C. G. Naumann, 1888.
The title page does not display a 'Zweite Auflage' statement.
Canvases 7-10 contain the Vorwort; canvas 11 is the internal work title and canvas 13 begins printed page 1.
Canvases 61-69 cover the terminal printed sequence through printed page 57; canvas 69 carries the terminal paragraph and holding stamp.
Canvas 70 is the printer leaf; canvases 71-73 are rear furniture and canvas 74 is the rear binding.

scholarly_text_history.source: Andreas Urs Sommer, Historischer und kritischer Kommentar zu Friedrich Nietzsches Werken, Band 6/1
bounded_findings: Nietzsche sent the printing manuscript to Naumann on 26 June 1888 and continued supplying additions.
By 9 August 1888 Nietzsche had already corrected galley proofs and was awaiting the proofs of the Nachschriften.
Printing was complete in September; official publication occurred on 22 September 1888.
The run comprised 1000 copies, with its second half designated 'Zweite Auflage'; the exact Bamberg title page carries no such designation.
